courses.title: Prosthetic Dentistry
courses.description: Complete dentures, removable partial dentures, immediate and overdentures, implant dentistry, maxillofacial prosthetics and denture-related problems.

topics.title: Complete Dentures: Principles and Clinical Stages
topics.summary: Edentulous anatomy, retention and stability, impressions, jaw relations and try-in.

material.heading: Principles
material.body: Tooth loss in Nigerian adults results mainly from periodontal disease and caries, and complete dentures (acrylic) remain the most common prosthetic treatment. After extraction, the alveolar ridge resorbs — faster in the mandible (about four times more than the maxilla), making lower dentures less stable. Denture-bearing areas: maxilla — the hard palate and residual ridge (primary support), with the posterior palatal seal at the vibrating line (junction of hard and soft palate); mandible — the buccal shelf (primary stress-bearing area) and retromolar pads. Retention (resistance to displacement away from tissues) depends on adhesion, cohesion, surface tension of saliva, peripheral seal, atmospheric pressure and muscular control; stability (resistance to horizontal forces) depends on ridge form and occlusion; support (resistance to vertical forces) depends on the area covered. The neutral zone is where forces from the tongue and cheeks are balanced — teeth should be placed there.
keyPoints: Posterior palatal seal at vibrating line

material.heading: Clinical stages
material.body: Stages: (1) assessment and primary impressions (alginate or impression compound in stock trays) → special (custom) trays; (2) secondary (master) impressions with border moulding (green stick compound) to record functional sulcus depth, using zinc oxide–eugenol paste or silicone; (3) jaw registration on wax occlusion rims — occlusal vertical dimension (OVD = rest vertical dimension minus freeway space of 2–4 mm), occlusal plane orientation (parallel to the interpupillary line and ala–tragus line), incisal level (about 1–2 mm of upper incisor visible at rest), centre line, and centric jaw relation; selection of tooth shade, shape and mould; (4) try-in of teeth set in wax (check aesthetics, phonetics — 'S' sounds and 'F/V' sounds, OVD, occlusion, patient approval); (5) processing, fitting and review with instructions (cleaning, removal at night, soaking, adaptation); (6) review appointments for adjustments. Errors: excessive OVD (clicking teeth, sore ridges, strained appearance), reduced OVD (angular cheilitis, collapsed face, reduced efficiency).

questions.explanation: Mandibular resorption is about four times greater.

questions.explanation: It resists vertical forces well.

questions.explanation: It improves retention.

questions.explanation: OVD = rest vertical dimension minus freeway space.

questions.stem: Border moulding during secondary impressions records:
options: Functional depth and width of the sulci
questions.explanation: It produces a peripheral seal.

questions.stem: An excessive occlusal vertical dimension may cause:

questions.explanation: Reduced OVD causes angular cheilitis.

Remove dentures at night and clean them daily
questions.explanation: This rests the tissues and reduces stomatitis.

topics.title: Removable Partial Dentures
topics.summary: Kennedy classification, components, design principles and materials.

material.heading: Classification and components
material.body: Kennedy classification of partially edentulous arches: Class I (bilateral free-end saddles), Class II (unilateral free-end saddle), Class III (unilateral bounded saddle), Class IV (single bounded anterior saddle crossing the midline); additional spaces are modifications (Applegate's rules — Class IV has no modifications; classification follows extractions/preparations). Components of a cobalt–chromium or acrylic RPD: saddles (bases) carrying artificial teeth, rests (occlusal, cingulum, incisal — provide support and transmit forces along the long axis), clasps (retainers engaging undercuts — occlusally approaching or gingivally approaching, e.g. I-bar; reciprocation opposite), connectors (major — palatal plate, strap, lingual bar, lingual plate; minor), and indirect retainers (resist rotation of free-end saddles). Surveying determines the path of insertion, undercuts and guide planes.

material.heading: Design and materials
material.body: Design follows a sequence: outline saddles, plan support (tooth-borne, mucosa-borne or combined), retention, bracing/reciprocation, connection and indirect retention. Tooth-supported designs are preferred where possible; free-end saddles are tooth–mucosa-borne and require extended bases, rests, and consideration of stress-breaking (RPI system — mesial rest, proximal plate, I-bar). Cobalt–chromium frameworks are thinner, stronger, more hygienic and better tolerated; acrylic partial dentures ('spoon dentures' for upper anterior teeth) are cheaper and common in Nigeria but gum-stripping designs damage the periodontium if not designed carefully. Flexible nylon dentures are aesthetic but difficult to adjust. Principles of periodontal health: keep gingival margins clear (at least 3–4 mm for lower lingual bars; 6 mm for upper connectors), plaque control and regular recall. Consider alternatives: shortened dental arch concept (a functional dentition with premolars may not need replacement of missing molars).

questions.stem: A partially edentulous arch with bilateral free-end saddles is Kennedy Class:
questions.explanation: Class II is unilateral free-end.

questions.stem: A single edentulous space anterior to remaining teeth that crosses the midline is Kennedy Class:
questions.explanation: Class IV has no modifications.

questions.stem: The component of an RPD that directs occlusal forces along the long axis of abutment teeth is the:
questions.explanation: Rests provide support.

questions.stem: Clasps provide retention by engaging:
questions.explanation: Flexible clasp tips sit in undercuts.

questions.stem: A surveyor is used to determine:
questions.explanation: It guides RPD design.

questions.stem: The RPI system for free-end saddles consists of a mesial rest, proximal plate and:
questions.explanation: It reduces torque on abutments.

questions.stem: An advantage of cobalt–chromium frameworks over acrylic partial dentures is:
options: Thinner, stronger and more hygienic design
questions.explanation: They cover less gingival tissue.

questions.stem: The shortened dental arch concept suggests that:
options: A dentition with intact anterior and premolar teeth may provide adequate function
All missing teeth must be replaced
questions.explanation: Missing molars need not always be replaced.

topics.title: Immediate Dentures, Overdentures and Denture Problems
topics.summary: Immediate and transitional dentures, overdentures, relines, denture stomatitis and complaints.

material.heading: Immediate dentures and overdentures
material.body: Immediate dentures are fitted immediately after extractions — maintaining appearance, function and speech, acting as a bandage and preserving face height; but they require relining as the ridge resorbs (soft reline early, hard reline or new denture after about 6 months) and cannot be tried in fully beforehand. Overdentures are complete dentures supported partly by retained roots (decoronated, root-filled and domed, or with attachments) or implants — retained roots preserve alveolar bone, proprioception and improve stability; caries and periodontal disease of the roots must be prevented (fluoride, cleaning). The two-implant-retained mandibular overdenture is considered a standard of care for edentulous mandibles (McGill consensus) where affordable. Copy (replica) dentures help elderly patients adapt to new dentures by preserving familiar features.
keyPoints: Immediate dentures: reline as ridge resorbs

material.heading: Denture problems
material.body: Denture stomatitis (chronic atrophic candidiasis) — erythema of the palatal mucosa under an upper denture — associated with continuous wear, poor denture hygiene, Candida albicans, and ill-fitting dentures; treat by removing dentures at night, cleaning and soaking (dilute hypochlorite for acrylic without metal, or chlorhexidine), antifungals (miconazole gel applied to the fitting surface, nystatin), and replacing poor dentures. Angular cheilitis (Candida and Staphylococcus; reduced OVD, haematinic deficiency). Denture hyperplasia (epulis fissuratum — overextended flanges) requires trimming and possibly excision. Common complaints: looseness (poor extension, resorption — reline or remake), pain (overextension, pressure spots — adjust with pressure-indicating paste), gagging, speech problems, food under dentures, and difficulty eating (adaptation takes time, especially lower dentures). Any non-healing ulcer under a denture after adjustment must be biopsied. Denture-related oral cancer risk is linked to chronic irritation combined with other risk factors.

questions.stem: An advantage of immediate dentures is that they:
options: Maintain appearance and function immediately after extractions
Can be fully tried in beforehand
Are cheaper than any other option
questions.explanation: Relining is needed as the ridge heals.

questions.stem: Retaining roots under an overdenture helps preserve:
questions.explanation: Bone resorbs less around retained roots.

questions.stem: The standard of care for edentulous mandibles according to the McGill consensus is:
options: Six implants and a fixed bridge
questions.explanation: It greatly improves stability.

questions.stem: Red palatal mucosa under an upper denture worn continuously suggests:
questions.explanation: Remove dentures at night and treat Candida.

questions.stem: Denture stomatitis is managed by denture hygiene and:
options: Antifungal therapy such as miconazole or nystatin
questions.explanation: Candida albicans is the main organism.

questions.stem: Folds of fibrous tissue around an overextended denture flange are:
questions.explanation: Trim the flange; excise if necessary.

questions.stem: Pressure spots on the fitting surface of a denture are located with:
questions.explanation: It shows where to adjust.

questions.stem: An ulcer under a denture that persists after adjustment should be:
questions.explanation: It may be malignant.

topics.title: Dental Implants
topics.summary: Osseointegration, assessment, surgical and prosthetic phases, and complications.

material.heading: Principles and assessment
material.body: Dental implants (usually commercially pure titanium or titanium alloy; zirconia alternatives) replace missing teeth via osseointegration — direct structural and functional connection between bone and implant surface (Brånemark). Assessment: medical history (uncontrolled diabetes, smoking, bisphosphonates/antiresorptives, head and neck radiotherapy, bleeding disorders, poor oral hygiene and untreated periodontitis are risk factors), patient expectations and cost (a major barrier in Nigeria), bone quantity and quality (Lekholm and Zarb classification), soft tissues, occlusion and aesthetics. Imaging: periapical/OPG, and cone-beam CT (CBCT) for 3D planning (proximity to the inferior alveolar canal — keep a 2 mm safety margin; maxillary sinus; mental foramen). Bone augmentation (guided bone regeneration, sinus lift) may be needed where bone is deficient. Minimum spacing: about 1.5 mm from adjacent teeth and 3 mm between implants.
keyPoints: 1.5 mm to teeth, 3 mm between implants

material.heading: Treatment and complications
material.body: Surgical protocols: two-stage (implant buried, uncovered after healing) or one-stage, with healing of about 3–6 months before loading (immediate loading in selected cases with high primary stability). Prosthetic options: single crowns (screw- or cement-retained), implant bridges, implant-retained overdentures (locator, ball or bar attachments), and full-arch fixed prostheses (e.g. 'All-on-4'). Success criteria include absence of mobility, pain, infection, radiolucency, and bone loss < 1.5 mm in the first year and < 0.2 mm annually thereafter (Albrektsson). Complications: surgical (nerve injury, haemorrhage — floor of mouth bleeding can threaten the airway, sinus perforation), early failure (lack of osseointegration — overheating bone, infection, micromovement), late failure (peri-implantitis — inflammation with bone loss; overload), and prosthetic (screw loosening, fracture of components, porcelain chipping). Maintenance: meticulous oral hygiene, regular reviews and radiographs.

questions.stem: Osseointegration refers to:
options: Direct structural and functional connection between bone and implant surface
questions.explanation: Described by Brånemark.

questions.stem: The most commonly used material for dental implants is:
questions.explanation: It is biocompatible and forms an oxide layer.

questions.stem: The imaging modality preferred for 3D implant planning is:
questions.explanation: It shows bone volume and vital structures.

questions.stem: A safety margin of about how much should be kept between an implant and the inferior alveolar canal?
questions.explanation: It prevents nerve injury.

questions.stem: A major risk factor for implant failure is:
questions.explanation: It impairs healing and increases peri-implantitis.

questions.stem: Conventional implants are typically left to heal before loading for about:
questions.explanation: Immediate loading is possible in selected cases.

questions.stem: Severe bleeding after implant placement in the anterior mandible can be dangerous because:
options: Floor of mouth haematoma can obstruct the airway
questions.explanation: Perforation of the lingual cortex can injure vessels.

questions.stem: Inflammation around a functioning implant with progressive bone loss is:
questions.explanation: It is a major cause of late failure.

topics.title: Maxillofacial Prosthetics and Special Prosthodontics
topics.summary: Obturators, facial prostheses, prosthodontics for the elderly, and denture materials care.

material.heading: Maxillofacial prosthetics
material.body: Maxillofacial prosthetics rehabilitate patients with defects from surgery (e.g. maxillectomy for tumours — ameloblastoma and malignancies common in Nigeria), trauma (gunshot and road crash injuries), noma sequelae, and congenital defects (cleft palate). Obturators close palatal defects: surgical obturator (placed at the time of surgery), interim obturator (during healing) and definitive obturator (hollow bulb to reduce weight) — restoring speech, swallowing (preventing nasal regurgitation) and aesthetics. Speech aids (palatal lift, speech bulb) help velopharyngeal insufficiency. Mandibular guidance prostheses help after mandibulectomy. Facial prostheses (ear, nose, orbit) made of silicone are retained by adhesives, spectacles or osseointegrated implants. Radiation stents and fluoride carriers protect patients undergoing radiotherapy. Multidisciplinary planning with surgeons improves outcomes.

material.heading: Geriatric prosthodontics and materials care
material.body: Nigeria's older population is growing; elderly edentulous patients may have reduced adaptability, xerostomia (medications), systemic diseases, cognitive impairment and limited manual dexterity. Strategies: copy dentures, simple designs, denture marking for identification in care settings, treating xerostomia (saliva substitutes), and involving carers in hygiene. Denture base materials: heat-cured PMMA (most common), cold-cured acrylic (repairs, relines), soft linings (silicone or acrylic-based — for thin mucosa or sharp ridges; deteriorate and harbour Candida). Denture cleaning: brush with soap or non-abrasive cleanser (not toothpaste — abrasive), soak in dilute hypochlorite (acrylic only — corrodes metal) or alkaline peroxide, and store moist. Denture fracture causes include fatigue (midline fracture of upper dentures), impact (dropping) and poor fit; repairs use cold-cured acrylic. Nutritional counselling helps denture wearers maintain a balanced diet.
